All safety claims
are machine-checked in Lean~4 under the cryptographic and operational
assumptions of Section~\ref{sec:assumptions} --- the core claims about
the imported Rust validator source itself, proved sound against the model
and re-used as the recursive-proof circuit (with circuit-backend faithfulness
a stated trust assumption), and today's key-rotation results at
model level.
notes: High-level prose assertion summarizing formal results.

tex_statement:
Beyond the classical counting argument, we prove that forged
chains advance at half real-time speed, and light-client safety is
proved directly in a timed model, against an adversary that harvests
coerced signatures stamped for any slot, so the recency check is a
machine-checked safety ingredient --- and we develop key rotation inside
consensus against an adversary who steals keys and keeps them forever:
three rotation modes with exactly stated operator and client duties.
notes: High-level prose assertion summarizing formal results.

tex_statement:
If the
certificate verifies and its tip is recent, the client may act on
everything $n$ blocks deep --- and that guarantee is a machine-checked
theorem about the shipped validator code
(\code{Rust.rust\_timed\_certified\_agreement}) under the assumptions of
Section~\ref{sec:assumptions}, not a design argument.
lean_statement:
@Rust.rust_timed_certified_agreement : ∀ {n : Aeneas.Std.U64},
  1 ≤ ↑n →
    ∀ {C : Type} (I : molt_petit.Crypto C) (crypto crypto' : C) {bad : MoltPetit.Model.ByzantineSlots}
      {log : MoltPetit.Model.TimedLog} {G : MoltPetit.Model.Block} {R : ℕ},
      MoltPetit.Model.TimedExecution (↑n) bad log G →
        MoltPetit.Model.ByzantineBounded (↑n) bad →
          (∀ ⦃B : MoltPetit.Model.Block⦄, Rust.RustSigned I crypto n B → ∃ r ≤ R, B ∈ log r) →
            (∀ (b : MoltPetit.Model.Block), Rust.RustSigned I crypto' n b → Rust.RustSigned I crypto n b) →
              (∀ (cert : molt_petit.Hash),
                  I.cert_verify crypto cert = Aeneas.Std.Result.ok Bool.true →
                    ∃ cl,
                      I.cert_claim crypto cert = Aeneas.Std.Result.ok cl ∧
                        MoltPetit.Model.GroundedCert (↑n) (Rust.RustSigned I crypto n) G (Rust.toModelClaim cl)) →
                (∀ (cert : molt_petit.Hash),
                    I.cert_verify crypto' cert = Aeneas.Std.Result.ok Bool.true →
                      ∃ cl,
                        I.cert_claim crypto' cert = Aeneas.Std.Result.ok cl ∧
                          MoltPetit.Model.GroundedCert (↑n) (Rust.RustSigned I crypto' n) G (Rust.toModelClaim cl)) →
                  ∀ {cert cert' : molt_petit.Hash} {suffix suffix' : molt_petit.SignedChain},
                    molt_petit.validate_certified_chain I n crypto (molt_petit.CertifiedChain.CC cert suffix) =
                        Aeneas.Std.Result.ok Bool.true →
                      molt_petit.validate_certified_chain I n crypto' (molt_petit.CertifiedChain.CC cert' suffix') =
                          Aeneas.Std.Result.ok Bool.true →
                        ∀ {sr1 sr1' : molt_petit.Block} {srtl srtl' : molt_petit.Chain},
                          molt_petit.strip_sigs suffix = Aeneas.Std.Result.ok (molt_petit.Chain.Cons sr1 srtl) →
                            molt_petit.strip_sigs suffix' = Aeneas.Std.Result.ok (molt_petit.Chain.Cons sr1' srtl') →
                              ∀ {sTip sTip' : MoltPetit.Model.Block},
                                (Rust.toModelBlock sr1 :: Rust.toModelChain srtl).getLast? = Option.some sTip →
                                  (Rust.toModelBlock sr1' :: Rust.toModelChain srtl').getLast? = Option.some sTip' →
                                    R ≤ sTip.slot + ↑n →
                                      R ≤ sTip'.slot + ↑n →
                                        ∀ {cl cl' : molt_petit.CertClaim},
                                          I.cert_claim crypto cert = Aeneas.Std.Result.ok cl →
                                            I.cert_claim crypto' cert' = Aeneas.Std.Result.ok cl' →
                                              ∀ {c c' : MoltPetit.Model.Chain},
                                                MoltPetit.Model.GroundedHistory (↑n) (Rust.RustSigned I crypto n) G
                                                    (Rust.toModelClaim cl) c →
                                                  MoltPetit.Model.GroundedHistory (↑n) (Rust.RustSigned I crypto' n) G
                                                      (Rust.toModelClaim cl') c' →
                                                    ∀ {h : ℕ},
                                                      h + ↑n <
                                                          List.length
                                                            (c ++ Rust.toModelBlock sr1 :: Rust.toModelChain srtl) →
                                                        h + ↑n <
                                                            List.length
                                                              (c' ++
                                                                Rust.toModelBlock sr1' :: Rust.toModelChain srtl') →
                                                          MoltPetit.Model.blockAt?
                                                              (c ++ Rust.toModelBlock sr1 :: Rust.toModelChain srtl) h =
                                                            MoltPetit.Model.blockAt?
                                                              (c' ++ Rust.toModelBlock sr1' :: Rust.toModelChain srtl')
                                                              h

tex_statement:
The validator is
one Rust file; it is \emph{imported} into Lean~4 (via Charon + Aeneas)
and proved sound against the model, so the core safety theorems are
about the code that runs (the rotation pins are checked at model level
today, Section~\ref{sec:impl}); the same source is re-used as the recursive-proof
circuit, so the prover proves the predicate that was verified (circuit-backend
faithfulness being a stated trust assumption rather than a Lean-verified equivalence); and a
separate TypeScript implementation is proved sound against that
\emph{same} Lean model --- which is what keeps the model
implementation-agnostic while it is developed by agentic coding.
notes: High-level prose assertion summarizing formal results.

tex_statement:
The loser recovers by
its mode's own discipline --- an in-band rotation in mode 1, a later
scheduled generation in mode 2, the next lockstep switch in mode 3 ---
at the price of its missed slots (operational discipline; mode 1's local
single-block production step under continued density coverage is checked
in the core, \code{liveness\_produce\_blockK}).
lean_statement:
@Molt.liveness_produce_blockK : ∀ {n Δconf me slot newId contentsHash keyIndex : ℕ}
  {bad : MoltPetit.Model.ByzantineSlots} {record : MoltPetit.Model.SlotRecord} {c : MoltPetit.Model.Chain}
  {tip : MoltPetit.Model.Block},
  MoltPetit.Model.ByzantineBounded n bad →
    MoltPetit.Model.validChainK n c = Bool.true →
      List.getLast? c = Option.some tip →
        tip.slot < slot →
          MoltPetit.Model.producerForSlot n slot = me →
            (∀ (s : ℕ), ∀ B ∈ record s, B.slot = s) →
              (∀ (u : ℕ),
                  tip.slot + 1 < u + n →
                    u + n ≤ slot + 1 →
                      MoltPetit.Model.HonestBlocksCover bad record
                        (c ++ [MoltPetit.Model.nextBlock slot newId contentsHash keyIndex tip]) u n) →
                MoltPetit.Model.keyFloor n c me ≤ keyIndex →
                  MoltPetit.Model.produceBlock? n me slot newId contentsHash keyIndex c =
                      Option.some (MoltPetit.Model.nextBlock slot newId contentsHash keyIndex tip) ∧
                    MoltPetit.Model.validChainK' n Δconf
                        (c ++ [MoltPetit.Model.nextBlock slot newId contentsHash keyIndex tip]) =
                      Bool.true

tex_statement:
A client that misses its cadence must stop acting and re-join from a
fresh trusted checkpoint, exactly as if it were new --- operational
discipline the theorems force rather than state: past the cadence the
theorems' fault-budget assumption becomes one no deployment can stand
behind --- quiet thefts accumulate until nothing satisfies it
(\code{no\_budget\_beyond}), and re-joining is a fresh trust event
outside the formal development.

(Mode 3's guarantees hold at the certificate presentation as well as for
full chains under the cumulative budget at depth $n$
(\code{lockstep\_recent\_certified\_suffix\_agreement}); lifting certificates
to per-generation erasure credit at depth $2n$ remains future work.

@Molt.lockstep_recent_certified_suffix_agreement : ∀ {n : ℕ},
  1 ≤ n →
    ∀ {rosterGen : ℕ → ℕ} {Sig sk pk : Type} {ops : MoltPetit.Model.SigOps Sig sk pk}
      {registry : MoltPetit.Model.KeyRegistry pk} {rented : MoltPetit.Model.ByzantineSlots} {Stolen : ℕ → ℕ → Prop}
      {honestSigned : ℕ → ℕ → Option MoltPetit.Model.Block} {now Δ : ℕ} {G : MoltPetit.Model.Block} {R T : ℕ},
      MoltPetit.Model.LockstepPackage n rosterGen ops registry rented Stolen honestSigned now Δ G R T →
        ∀ {cl cl' : MoltPetit.Model.CertClaim} {g g' : ℕ},
          MoltPetit.Model.GroundedCertLock n (MoltPetit.Model.SignedDeclared n ops registry) G cl g →
            MoltPetit.Model.GroundedCertLock n (MoltPetit.Model.SignedDeclared n ops registry) G cl' g' →
              ∀ {s₁ s₁' : MoltPetit.Model.Block} {srest srest' : MoltPetit.Model.Chain}
                {sTip sTip' : MoltPetit.Model.Block},
                (s₁ :: srest).getLast? = Option.some sTip →
                  (s₁' :: srest').getLast? = Option.some sTip' →
                    s₁.height = cl.tipHeight + 1 ∧ cl.tipSlot < s₁.slot ∧ s₁.prev = Option.some cl.tipId →
                      MoltPetit.Model.linksOk (s₁ :: srest) = Bool.true →
                        (∀ (u : ℕ),
                            ↑cl.tipSlot + 2 - ↑n ≤ ↑u →
                              u + n ≤ sTip.slot + 1 →
                                MoltPetit.Model.quorum n ≤ MoltPetit.Model.windowCount (cl.tail ++ s₁ :: srest) u n) →
                          MoltPetit.Model.lockstepFrom n cl.tipSlot g (s₁ :: srest) = Bool.true →
                            (∀ B ∈ s₁ :: srest, MoltPetit.Model.SignedDeclared n ops registry B) →
                              s₁'.height = cl'.tipHeight + 1 ∧
                                  cl'.tipSlot < s₁'.slot ∧ s₁'.prev = Option.some cl'.tipId →
                                MoltPetit.Model.linksOk (s₁' :: srest') = Bool.true →
                                  (∀ (u : ℕ),
                                      ↑cl'.tipSlot + 2 - ↑n ≤ ↑u →
                                        u + n ≤ sTip'.slot + 1 →
                                          MoltPetit.Model.quorum n ≤
                                            MoltPetit.Model.windowCount (cl'.tail ++ s₁' :: srest') u n) →
                                    MoltPetit.Model.lockstepFrom n cl'.tipSlot g' (s₁' :: srest') = Bool.true →
                                      (∀ B ∈ s₁' :: srest', MoltPetit.Model.SignedDeclared n ops registry B) →
                                        now ≤ sTip.slot + Δ →
                                          now ≤ sTip'.slot + Δ →
                                            ∀ {i i' : ℕ} {B B' : MoltPetit.Model.Block},
                                              MoltPetit.Model.blockAt? (s₁ :: srest) i = Option.some B →
                                                MoltPetit.Model.blockAt? (s₁' :: srest') i' = Option.some B' →
                                                  cl.tipHeight + 1 + i = cl'.tipHeight + 1 + i' →
                                                    i + n < (s₁ :: srest).length →
                                                      i' + n < (s₁' :: srest').length → B = B'

tex_statement:
Erasure's per-generation credit against the budget is machine-checked:
under a per-generation census --- for each generation $j$ separately, at
most $T$ seats whose generation-$j$ key is stolen --- the same agreement
holds at confirmation depth $2n$ instead of $n$ (at equal tip heights,
\code{lockstep\_client\_safety\_gen}; at unequal heights the lower
chain's $2n$-deep block lies on the taller,
\code{lockstepGen\_recent\_tip\_ancestor\_mem}), and with no
shared-genesis hypothesis; the
cumulative, depth-$n$ form remains available.

@Molt.lockstep_client_safety_gen : ∀ {n : ℕ},
  1 ≤ n →
    ∀ {rosterGen : ℕ → ℕ} {Sig sk pk : Type} {ops : Molt.SigOps Sig sk pk} {registry : Molt.KeyRegistry pk}
      {rented : Molt.ByzantineSlots} {Stolen : ℕ → ℕ → Prop} {honestSigned : Molt.SigningLog} {now Δ : ℕ}
      {G : Molt.Block} {R T : ℕ},
      Molt.LockstepPackageGen n rosterGen ops registry rented Stolen honestSigned now Δ G R T →
        ∀ {sc sc' : Molt.SignedChain Sig},
          Molt.validSignedChainLock n ops registry sc = Bool.true →
            Molt.validSignedChainLock n ops registry sc' = Bool.true →
              ∀ {sTip sTip' : Molt.Block},
                List.getLast? (Molt.stripSigs sc) = Option.some sTip →
                  List.getLast? (Molt.stripSigs sc') = Option.some sTip' →
                    now ≤ sTip.slot + Δ →
                      now ≤ sTip'.slot + Δ →
                        2 * n < List.length (Molt.stripSigs sc) →
                          2 * n < List.length (Molt.stripSigs sc') →
                            sTip.height = sTip'.height →
                              ∀ {B B' : Molt.Block},
                                Molt.blockAt? (Molt.stripSigs sc) (List.length (Molt.stripSigs sc) - 1 - 2 * n) =
                                    Option.some B →
                                  Molt.blockAt? (Molt.stripSigs sc') (List.length (Molt.stripSigs sc') - 1 - 2 * n) =
                                      Option.some B' →
                                    B = B'

                                                        sTip.height = sTip'.height →
                                                          ∀ {B B' : Molt.Block},
                                                            Molt.blockAt? (Molt.stripSigs sc)
                                                                  (List.length (Molt.stripSigs sc) - 1 - n) =

tex_statement:
The assumption
bundles: \emph{(a) custody} --- honest nodes sign only through their
honest signing path, and their secret keys never leave them; \emph{(b)
unforgeability} --- no one can produce a valid signature on a message the
key holder never signed, even after obtaining signatures on messages of
their own choosing (the standard EUF-CMA notion); here the attacker gets
exactly that power at every bad slot, whose producer can be made to sign
anything; and \emph{(c) the timed signing discipline} --- at a bad real slot
the producer's key signs arbitrarily many blocks with any stamp in its
residue class (\code{key\_match}); an honest real slot signs only its own
current block (\code{honest\_stamp}) and at most once (\code{honest\_once});
and every producer signature accepted by the verifier at real slot $R$
was produced at some real slot no later than $R$ (\code{hbridge},
causality plus EUF-CMA).

The id-formation contract of Section~\ref{sec:protocol} ensures that a block
is signed only once its parent is available (\code{chain\_order}).

The id-formation contract
of Section~\ref{sec:protocol} appears as the field \code{chain\_order}: a
block can be signed only once its parent is \emph{available}, because the
parent's id preimage contains the parent's signature, and predicting
another party's signature on a known message is exactly an EUF-CMA
forgery.

\begin{theorem}[Forged suffixes advance at half speed; Lean
\code{forged\_time\_bound}]\label{thm:forge}
In the timed model with the fault budget: let a valid chain be available
at real slot $r_{\mathrm{now}}$, let $F$ be one of its blocks, first
signed at real slot $r_0$, and let every chain block past $F$'s slot have
been signed only at bad real slots (the suffix above $F$ is forged by
coercion). Then
\[
\quorum \cdot \left\lfloor
  \tfrac{\mathit{tip.slot} - F.\mathit{slot}}{n} \right\rfloor
\;\le\;
\fmax \cdot \left( \left\lfloor \tfrac{r_{\mathrm{now}} - r_0}{n}
  \right\rfloor + 1 \right).
\]
Since $\quorum \approx 2\fmax$: forging a suffix that spans $s$ slots
takes about $2s$ real slots. The from-genesis corollary
(\code{forged\_chain\_time\_bound}) reads: a fully forged chain claiming
tip slot $s$ cannot exist before real slot ${\approx}\,2s$. (The Lean
statements carry non-degeneracy side conditions --- $n \ge 2$, $F$ not
the first block; a forged span under one window makes the
bound trivially true, ruling nothing out.)
\end{theorem}

          ∀ {c : Molt.Chain},

              G.prev = Option.none →
                ∀ {rNow : ℕ},

                    ∀ {k₀ : ℕ},

ancestor, and Theorem~\ref{thm:lc} is the machine-checked statement of

\begin{theorem}[Scheduled safety under horizon budget; Lean
\code{sched\_recent\_tip\_ancestor\_agreement\_horizon},\hfil\penalty0
\code{sched\_recent\_tip\_ancestor\_mem\_horizon}]\label{thm:sched}
Under the scheduled validator (\code{validSignedChainSched}) on both
chains; the scheduled signature surface (\code{SchedUnforgeable},
recency-scoped with $\mathit{now}$, $\Delta$); hash injectivity over
declared-version signatures (Assumption~\ref{ass:hash}, \code{SignedHashInjective});
the corruption budget \code{ByzantineBoundedFrom}~$H$~$n$~(\code{badSched} \dots)
--- at most $\fmax$ bad slots in every $n$-slot window starting at or after
a horizon $H$; the horizon side conditions $H + n \le \mathit{tip}.\mathit{slot} + 1$
for both tips; recency $\mathit{now} \le \mathit{tip}.\mathit{slot} + \Delta$
for both tips; sufficient chain length $n < \mathit{length}$ (\code{hLong},
for both chains at equal heights; for the lower chain at unequal heights);
and the tip-height relation of each form (\code{hTipHeight}: equal
heights; \code{hLe}: the first tip no higher). Then two accepted chains agree: at equal tip heights, on the block $n$ below
each tip; at unequal tip heights, the lower chain's $n$-deep ancestor block
is a block of the taller chain, at least $n$ deep there.
There is no shared-genesis hypothesis: genesis agreement is a consequence
(\code{sched\_recent\_genesis\_agreement\_horizon}).
The global-budget \code{scheduled\_client\_safety} is the corollary at
any $H$ (\code{byzantineBoundedFrom\_of\_bounded}).
No anchor, no sync rule, no confirmation wait: the client holds a clock
and the constant $\mathit{gen}$, and may stay offline arbitrarily long.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Liveness; Lean \code{production\_liveness},
\code{global\_liveness}]\label{thm:live}
\emph{Local:} under the fault budget and honest delivery
(Assumptions~\ref{ass:budget} and~\ref{ass:delivery}), when a slot
arrives that belongs to an honest producer holding an accepted chain,
production succeeds --- the extension passes the same validator everyone
runs. \emph{Global:} a synchronous honest run within the budget (over
the run's span; each honest block reaches the next honest producer
within its slot) is
validator-accepted with one block per honest slot, so the chain reaches
any height and every block eventually becomes $n$-deep.
\end{theorem}

@Molt.production_liveness : ∀ {n me slot newId contentsHash keyIndex : ℕ} {bad : MoltPetit.Model.ByzantineSlots}
  {record : MoltPetit.Model.SlotRecord} {c : MoltPetit.Model.Chain} {tip : MoltPetit.Model.Block},
  MoltPetit.Model.ByzantineBounded n bad →
    MoltPetit.Model.validChain n c = Bool.true →
      List.getLast? c = Option.some tip →
        tip.slot < slot →
          MoltPetit.Model.producerForSlot n slot = me →
            (∀ (s : ℕ), ∀ B ∈ record s, B.slot = s) →
              (∀ (u : ℕ),
                  tip.slot + 1 < u + n →
                    u + n ≤ slot + 1 →
                      MoltPetit.Model.HonestBlocksCover bad record
                        (c ++ [MoltPetit.Model.nextBlock slot newId contentsHash keyIndex tip]) u n) →
                MoltPetit.Model.produceBlock? n me slot newId contentsHash keyIndex c =
                  Option.some (MoltPetit.Model.nextBlock slot newId contentsHash keyIndex tip)

            (MoltPetit.Model.badSlotsIn (fun s => s ∉ g.slot :: ss) u n).card ≤ MoltPetit.Model.maxByzantine n) →

                            (∀ (u : ℕ),

                                    Molt.quorum n ≤ Molt.windowCount (cl.tail ++ s₁ :: srest) u n) →
